clue.text: Famous artwork has legs on top

parts.note: something that has legs keeps going, so it lasts
the upper one is the one on top

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a celebrated painting has its legs placed at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has legs' is an idiom for staying power: a story with legs lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci's mural of Christ's final meal in Milan is one of the most celebrated paintings in the world.

clue.text: Church leaders are implicated in suspicious sexual activity

indicators.note: being implicated in something puts these letters inside the other word

parts.note: leery means wary or suspicious
the leading letters of Church, also its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Clergy are caught up in a sex scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lechery is excessive or offensive lust, so it names a kind of sexual behaviour.

clue.text: Old photograph found within Milanese piano

indicators.note: the answer is found within the words, running across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Milanese and the start of piano

explanation.surface: An antique photo turns up inside a piano from Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the brown tint of early photographic prints, and by extension such a print itself.

clue.text: 10 down, drunk and extremely high

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the answer to the clue at 10 down

explanation.surface: A reveller is drunk and very high indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The two long downs are anagrams of each other, each clued by the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratosphere is a high layer of the atmosphere, so the adjective means sky-high or enormous.

clue.text: Twisted plaits framing Pippi Longstocking, ultimately!

definitions.text: Twisted plaits framing Pippi Longstocking, ultimately!

indicators.note: the rearranged word frames the other letter
twisted means the letters of plaits are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be twisted

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word of the name

parts.note: the last letter of each word of the heroine's name

explanation.surface: Twisted braids frame the face of Pippi Longstocking.
explanation.walkthrough: Pippi Longstocking, the Swedish children's heroine, is famous for her two stiff braids sticking out sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes braided hair worn hanging at each side, the hairstyle Pippi is known for.

clue.text: Catch parent in a mix-up

indicators.note: a mix-up jumbles the letters of parent

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be mixed up

explanation.surface: A mother or father gets caught in some confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to trick them into a trap, so it means to catch them.

clue.text: "Bound to go downhill!" (pessimist's starting point)

parts.note: skiing is going downhill on snow

indicators.note: the starting point of a word is its first letter, here of pessimist's

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A gloomy person's opening remark: everything is bound to go downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to' in the quoted gloom, but it is the verb meaning a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound and to skip are both light, springing movements, so the words are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Surprisingly, Nobel Peace Prize winner is more prone to smooching?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Henry ..., US Secretary of State, who won the prize in 1973
second meaning: read as ..., a comparative of a made-up adjective kissing

explanation.walkthrough: Surprisingly is a nudge that the statesman's name can be split as a jokey comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the diplomat honoured for the Vietnam ceasefire also reads as a whimsical comparison of kissing tendencies.

clue.text: Typeset Asimov excerpt for money, once

indicators.note: an excerpt is a passage taken from within the words

parts.note: the letters run from inside Typeset into Asimov

explanation.surface: Someone typesets an extract from Isaac Asimov in exchange for payment.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was the currency unit of Spain before the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Legally protect Gothic novel involving endless material for funeral

indicators.note: the rearranged word involves, that is wraps around, the other piece
novel means new, so the letters of Gothic are made new in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for the funeral material is dropped

parts.note: a pyre is the heap of wood burned at a funeral

explanation.surface: A legal move to protect a Gothic novel that features a funeral pyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gothic novel' reads as a book, but 'novel' is the signal to rearrange 'Gothic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, copyright means to secure the exclusive legal rights to a work.

clue.text: Expels American in overtime, at completion of pass

indicators.note: the American abbreviation sits inside the overtime abbreviation
the completion of a word is its final letter, here of pass

parts.note: its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A sports report: an American sent off in overtime at the end of a passing play.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to drive or push them out, the same as expelling them.

clue.text: 3 scattered locations for music

indicators.note: scattered means the letters are spread out into a new order

parts.note: the answer to the clue at 3 down

explanation.surface: Places where music is played are scattered about.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestra pits are the sunken areas before a stage where theatre and opera musicians play.

clue.text: Require improved ax, etc.

indicators.note: improved suggests the letters are reworked into something better

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be reworked

explanation.surface: A need for a better axe and other tools.
explanation.walkthrough: AX is the American spelling of axe.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact something is to demand it as due, so it is a synonym of require in that sense.

clue.text: A government agent ferociously hits Emma Goldman, perhaps

parts.note: taken as written
a narc is an American narcotics officer

indicators.note: ferociously suggests the letters of hits are violently thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A federal officer violently attacks the famous radical Emma Goldman.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma Goldman (1869-1940) was a famous anarchist writer and activist in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldman was a leading political radical who rejected all state authority, the textbook example of that ideology.

clue.text: Charles returns with amazing deals from neighborhood clearance

indicators.note: returns means the name is turned back to front

parts.note: Ray Charles, the singer, gives his first name

indicators.note: amazing hints that the letters of deals are dazed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Charles comes back with wonderful bargains from a local clear-out.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles is the surname of the singer Ray Charles, so the name supplies his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage-style sale of unwanted household goods held on the lawn is a way to clear things out locally.

clue.text: Incorrectly label your color

indicators.note: incorrectly means the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to mislabel your paint colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, vivid shade, so it is an example of a colour.

clue.text: Beginning to load Borders' shelves

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of load

parts.note: its first letter is used
borders are edges

explanation.surface: Starting to stock the shelves at the bookstore chain Borders.
explanation.walkthrough: Borders was an American bookstore chain, which is what the capital letter suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow flat projection, much like a shelf along a wall or rock face.

clue.text: Providing more weapons to back Chinese dynasty

parts.note: the rear is the back
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: Rearming troops to support an imperial Chinese dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearming means supplying arms again, giving fresh weapons to forces.

clue.text: Tipsy cheapskate has a soul

indicators.note: the phrase has the answer within it, across its words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of Tipsy into cheapskate

explanation.surface: A drunk miser turns out to have a soul after all.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human spirit or mind, from the Greek word for breath and soul.

clue.text: Scroll to see father cooking syrup

parts.note: pa is father

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of syrup are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be cooked

explanation.surface: Instructions to scroll down to find Dad making syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptian scrolls were made from papyrus reed, so the word names such a document.

clue.text: Federal bureau to launch prison section

parts.note: the DEA is the US Drug Enforcement Administration
to launch something is to throw it

explanation.surface: A federal agency is about to launch a section of a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Death row is the block of a prison where inmates sentenced to execution are held.

clue.text: Former mobile device's image on traffic sign?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Sony portable cassette player of the 1980s
second meaning: the walking figure lit on a pedestrian crossing signal

explanation.walkthrough: The pedestrian signal shows a figure walking, a walk man.
explanation.definitionFit: The trademark portable stereo, now outdated, shares its name with a description of the striding figure on crossing lights.

clue.text: Rabies outbreak in the country

indicators.note: an outbreak breaks the letters of rabies out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: News of a rabies outbreak in the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a Balkan nation in southeastern Europe with Belgrade as its capital.

clue.text: Organized labor splits fruit with victim of global warming

indicators.note: the rearranged word splits the fruit by sitting in its middle

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: organized means the letters of labor are arranged anew

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade union causes a division over fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organized labor' looks like a trade union, but 'Organized' is the signal to rearrange 'labor'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic bear that hunts from sea ice is the emblematic animal threatened by melting ice from climate change.

clue.text: Heavy metal piece (vinyl, originally): "Inside a Zero"

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: inside means the letter goes within the word for zero

parts.note: nil is zero

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of vinyl

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A heavy metal track on vinyl from an album called Inside a Zero.
explanation.walkthrough: Anvil is also a Canadian heavy metal band, so the surface reads as a record listing.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's anvil is a massive block of iron on which hot metal is hammered.

clue.text: 501 ad, say

parts.note: each digit as a letter: 5 as the Roman numeral V, 0 as O, 1 as the Roman numeral I
AD, Anno Domini, is now often written CE, Common Era

explanation.surface: A date in the year 501 AD is given.
explanation.walkthrough: The digits are read one by one, and AD dating is swapped for its secular equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to express it aloud, so voice means say as a verb.

clue.text: Leftover fried rice contains a bit of lemon

indicators.note: the rearranged word contains the other letter
fried means the letters of rice are cooked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be fried

indicators.note: a bit of a word is here its first letter, from lemon

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Yesterday's fried rice with a little lemon in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from the past, a remnant left over from an earlier time.

clue.text: Raise initial grade of review in maths, for example

indicators.note: the first letter is a grade, and raising a C grade makes it a B

parts.note: a critical review is a criticism

explanation.surface: A request to bump up the first mark given to a maths review.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say math; maths is the British form, so the word itself is the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Briticism is a word or idiom peculiar to British English, and maths is one.

clue.text: Stalk nine from Queens in retreat

indicators.note: a team in retreat falls back, so its name is read backwards

parts.note: the New York Mets baseball team, a nine, plays in Queens

explanation.surface: Someone tracks nine people from Queens as they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: A baseball team has nine players, so a nine is a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem is the main stalk of a plant, the noun sense here.

clue.text: Adult male's preceding adolescent, grabbing game and tropical fruit

indicators.note: the first part comes before the next one
the man's word grabs the game by holding it inside

parts.note: a man's, with the possessive s
Go is the Asian board game
a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: A grown man is ahead of a teenager, grabbing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangosteen is a purple-skinned fruit from Southeast Asian tropical trees with sweet white segments.
